newsitem.title: USA: Natgas futures end with technical, weather gains.
newsitem.headline: Natgas futures end with technical, weather gains.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures mostly ended with gains Tuesday in a moderate session, with spot-November leading the way on technical buying and reports of some weather-related strength in the cash, sources said.
November rallied 6.9 cents to close at $2.438 per million British thermal units. December settled 4.9 cents higher at $2.605. Most other deferreds ended steady to up 5.9 cents.

"We hit technical stops over $2.40, and when they couldn't break it down late, locals bought it up. But I'm not sure how much further we can go with futures at a 20-cent premium to cash," said one Midwest trader.

Despite the restoration of most of the U.S. Gulf gas output cut this week by Tropical Storm Josephine, cool Midwest and Northeast weather, record heat out West and steady storage buying all combined to tighten the cash.
Technically, traders said November's close Tuesday above $2.43 could set up a test of next resistance in the $2.50 area. Support was pegged around $2.30.
Cash sources said Gulf Coast prices firmed slightly Monday to the high-teens. Midcon pipes gained more than a nickel to the low-$2 area. Gas at New York city gate was unchanged in the mid-$2.40s.
The 12-month Henry Hub strip rose 1.2 cents to $2.237. NYMEX said 43,550 Hub contracts traded, up from Monday's revised tally of 37,448.
NYMEX November Alberta natgas settled up four cents at $1.085, while deferreds closed steady to three cents higher. NYMEX said 243 Alberta contracts traded.
NYMEX November Permian natgas was untraded but also settled with a four-cent gain at $2.05. Deferreds ended up by one to four cents. NYMEX said 90 Permian lots changed hands versus 19 on Monday.

On the KCBT, November settled six cents higher at $1.97, while deferreds ended up by two to 4.5 cents. The East/West spread widened by 0.9 cent to 28.8 cents (NYMEX premium). KCBT said 348 contracts traded, up from Monday's total of 93.
